'''Business and economy'''
*[[German economic crisis (2022–present)|German economic crisis]]
**[[Lufthansa]] staff conduct a one-day [[general strike|strike]] to protest the airline's [[cost reduction|cost-cutting]] measures, grounding at least 460 flights and affecting nearly 70,000 passengers. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-lufthansa-strike-grounds-hundreds-of-flights/a-75922927 (DW)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/hundreds-lufthansa-flights-cancelled-pilots-cabin-crew-walk-out-2026-02-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025–26 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season]]
**At least 31 people are killed, 36 others are injured, and several are missing as [[Cyclone Gezani]] makes landfall in [[Madagascar]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/madagascar-cyclone-kills-dozens-causes-widespread-damage/a-75921072 (DW)]
*[[2026 Sarajevo tram derailment]]
**A tram derails in [[Sarajevo]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], killing one person and injuring four. [https://sarajevotimes.com/a-young-man-was-killed-and-four-people-were-injured-in-a-tram-accident/ (''Sarajevo Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Environmental policy of the second Trump administration]]
**[[United States]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] revokes the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]]'s [[Regulation of greenhouse gases under the Clean Air Act|2009 endangerment finding]], which classified [[greenhouse gas]]es as a threat to [[Health in the United States|public health]] and formed the legal basis for [[Climate change policy of the United States|federal climate regulations]], and concurrently rescinds [[United States vehicle emission standards|vehicle emission standards]]. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/2/13/trump-dismantles-legal-basis-for-us-climate-rules-0653 (AFP via ABS-CBN)]
*[[Greenhouse gas emissions by China]]
**The [[Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air]] reports that [[China]]'s [[Greenhouse gas emissions|carbon dioxide emissions]] remained flat or declined slightly in 2025 by about 0.3%, marking the first full calendar year in which emissions in China did not rise despite increasing [[Electricity sector in China|energy demand]], largely due to expanded [[Renewable energy in China|renewable energy]] capacity. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260212-china-carbon-emissions-flat-or-falling-in-2025-analysis (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Japan relations]]
**[[2025–2026 China–Japan diplomatic crisis]]
***The [[Japan]]ese [[Fisheries Agency (Japan)|fisheries agency]] seize a [[Fishing industry in China|Chinese fishing]] [[Fishing vessel|vessel]] and arrest its captain who failed to stop for inspection within [[Exclusive economic zone of Japan|Japan's exclusive economic zone]] off [[Nagasaki Prefecture]], marking the first such seizure since 2022. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/308969/japan-confirms-seized-chinese-fishing-boat-arrested-skipper (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[Dominican Republic–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] announces the closure of its [[Drug Enforcement Administration]] office in [[Santo Domingo]], [[Dominican Republic]], citing unspecified [[Corruption in the United States|corruption]] concerns within the mission. [https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2026/02/12/us-shutters-dominican-anti-drug-office-corruption-claims/ (AFP via ''Jamaica Observer'')]
*[[Kenya–Somalia relations]], [[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Kenya]]n [[President of Kenya|president]] [[William Ruto]] announces the reopening of the country's [[Mandera]] border post with [[Somalia]] in April, ending a 15-year closure imposed in 2011 following [[Timeline of al-Shabaab-related events|attacks]] attributed to [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]], after earlier reopening plans were delayed due to renewed violence near the border. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/africa/kenya-to-reopen-border-with-somalia-after-15-year-closure (AFP via ''Daily Sabah'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Connections of Jeffrey Epstein]]
**Former [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[Prime Minister of Norway|prime minister]] [[Thorbjørn Jagland]] is charged with gross [[Corruption in Norway|corruption]] over connections with American [[sex trafficker]] [[Jeffrey Epstein]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5yqr8eggvwo (BBC News)]
*Two people are killed and another is injured in a shooting at a [[South Carolina State University]] dormitory building in [[Orangeburg, South Carolina|Orangeburg]], [[South Carolina]], United States. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/two-dead-one-injured-shooting-south-carolina-state-university-campus-rcna258931 (NBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangladeshi general election]]
**[[Bangladeshis]] vote to elect members of the [[Jatiya Sangsad]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cd03znje072t (BBC News)]
*[[2026 Barbadian general election]]
**Projections of early morning results indicate that incumbent [[Barbados|Barbadian]] [[Prime Minister of Barbados|prime minister]] [[Mia Mottley]] will win a third term in office, with the [[Barbados Labour Party]] securing all 30 seats in the [[House of Assembly of Barbados|House of Assembly]] for the third election in a row. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/barbados-pm-mia-mottley-wins-third-election-with-clean-sweep-2026-02-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Internet in Portugal]]
**[[Portugal]]'s [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|parliament]] approves, on [[first reading]], a [[Law of Portugal#Legislative system|bill]] requiring explicit parental consent for children aged 13 to 16 to access [[social media]], mandating [[Age verification system|age verification]] through the state's [[electronic identification]] system and imposing fines of up to 2 percent of global revenue on [[List of social networking services|companies]] that fail to comply. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/portugal-approves-restrictions-social-media-access-children-2026-02-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Winter Olympics]]
**The [[International Olympic Committee]] disqualifies [[National Olympic Committee of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[skeleton racer]] [[Vladyslav Heraskevych]] from [[Skeleton at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's|competing]] due to his helmet, which has images of Ukrainian athletes killed by [[Russian Armed Forces]]. [https://www.npr.org/2026/02/12/nx-s1-5712159/ukrainian-olympian-disqualified-over-images-of-war-dead-on-his-helmet (NPR)]
